title: Security Postmortem: Audit Log Gaps and Key Rotation Failure During SSO Rollout
creator: Asha Mehra
description:
Summary:
During a staged SSO (SAML) rollout to a subset of enterprise customers on 2026-02-25, we experienced two related failures: a key-rotation job failed to complete for the tenant KMS keys, and the audit-log ingestion pipeline dropped a window of events. The combined effect was a 37-minute authentication degradation for affected tenants (SSO redirects intermittently failed) and missing audit records covering ~2.3 hours for three customers required by ongoing compliance reviews.

Impact:
- 3 enterprise customers reported SSO failures between 09:12 and 09:49 UTC. Some authentication retries succeeded; others got 500/timeout responses.
- Audit logs for the period 07:15–09:35 UTC are incomplete for the three customers; downstream compliance exports show gaps used during SOC review.
- No data exfiltration detected. No customer secrets were exposed.

Detection & Response:
- Pager alerted on SSO error rate spike at 09:18 UTC. On-call (Tomás) triaged and traced failures to KMS-backed token signing calls returning 500s.
- At 09:27 UTC, we observed the audit ingestion service (aud-collector) experiencing frequent restarts due to a config reload introduced in the SSO rollout recipe. Collector restarted with a transient state where the last-processed checkpoint was overwritten, causing duplication-and-loss behavior in the Kafka consumer group.
- Workarounds applied: manual rollback of the SSO rollout config (09:35 UTC) and temporary disabling of the noisy config reload (09:40 UTC). Audit ingestion resumed but missing-window required backfill.

Root cause analysis (summary):
1) Key rotation job race condition: The asynchronous key-rotation worker attempted to rotate tenant signing keys while the SSO deployment was updating trust metadata. A 500 from the cloud KMS API was treated as success in one code path because of a malformed success-check; the worker recorded a new key-version id without a corresponding key material write, leading to verification failures during SSO token issuance.
2) Audit ingestion checkpoint regression: The recent change to aud-collector added a hot-reload that resets in-memory checkpoint pointers during config validation. When the collector restarted, its checkpoint commit logic failed to rehydrate last-processed offsets for certain tenant partitions. Combined with a short retention on raw logs in the temporary pipeline, this caused irrecoverable gaps for ~2.3 hours.
3) Insufficient integration test coverage: The staging pipeline and the key-rotation e2e test matrix did not include a simultaneous SSO metadata update + key rotation scenario, and there was no synthetic end-to-end SSO smoke test validating token signing + audit emission under transient KMS errors.

What went well:
- Pager escalation and on-call response followed runbook and restored user-facing failures within 37 minutes of initial alert.
- Cross-team coordination (infra, security, SSO team, compliance) enabled a targeted rollback and a prioritized backfill plan.

Action items (owner — due):
- A1: Patch key-rotation worker to treat KMS 5xx as retryable and add atomic commit semantics (write-then-record). Include unit tests for failure paths. Owner: Tomás Rivera. Due: 2026-03-05.
- A2: Add durable checkpointing to aud-collector: commit offsets to durable store before applying config reloads; add migration to rehydrate offsets on restart. Owner: Priya Patel. Due: 2026-03-12.
- A3: Backfill missing audit records for affected tenants using raw source logs and rehydrate downstream exports; produce a compliance attestation for impacted customers. Owner: Compliance; Support liaison: Mei Chen. Due: 2026-03-08.
- A4: Add an e2e staging test that simulates: config hot-reload, concurrent key rotation, transient KMS 5xx, and verifies both SSO token issuance and audit emission. Owner: QA — Eric Blue. Due: 2026-03-15.
- A5: Update SSO rollout playbook and release checklist to require staging key rotation smoke test and KMS error injection prior to production rollout. Owner: SSO PM — Lina Park. Due: 2026-03-10.
- A6: Increase raw audit log retention in the temporary pipeline from 24h to 72h to give more backfill buffer while durable checkpointing work is implemented. Owner: Infra — Kevin O'Donnell. Due: 2026-03-02.
- A7: Run a tenant-wide key integrity audit and rotate any keys that have inconsistent metadata. Owner: Security Ops — Asha Mehra. Due: 2026-03-18.
- A8: Update incident runbook with steps for verifying KMS semantics, how to force-safe rollback, and a mapping for audit partitions to tenant IDs. Owner: Reliability Docs — Nora Kim. Due: 2026-03-04.

Residual risk and mitigations:
- Residual: Until durable checkpointing is in place, short-lived collector restarts could still create small gaps under high churn.
- Mitigation: Temporary increase in retention (A6), and a canary that injects a restart into staging daily to exercise recovery (A4).

Follow-ups & next steps:
- Technical review session scheduled 2026-03-11 with infra, SSO, security, and compliance to walk the patches and backfill plan.
- Deliver compliance attestation to the three affected customers and legal (due 2026-03-08).
- Close loop with sales/CS: proactive outreach to affected accounts and crediting per support policy.

Attachments / links:
- GitHub PRs: PR#8123 (key-rotation guardrails), PR#8140 (aud-collector checkpointing), PR#8165 (staging e2e harness)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/company/security/sso-rollout-runbook
- Incident timeline dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/SSO/ingestion-incident-2026-02-25

Conclusion:
This incident highlights the coupling risk between deployment workflows (SSO metadata changes), key management, and audit collection. The action items above eliminate the immediate correctness bugs and add test and process controls to prevent recurrence. We must prioritize A1, A2, and A3 to meet compliance commitments and reduce residual risk.
